transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Two taps. That's me. If you're hearing this, I missed a check-in, and you're sitting in my chair because nobody else wanted the paperwork.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He missed three. He told me once: one check-in is weather, two is trouble, three is worry. I've been worried since Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Sparrow. You fly the pattern too low and too fast, and I never fixed it, because it's the only thing you do without asking permission.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Command calls it desertion. They made me say the word on the net. I said it. I'm not saying it again.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: If I miss your checkout, fly the pattern anyway. The sky will still be there.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: An empty chair and a checkout nobody's signing. Fine. I'll fly the pattern.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The bombers wore our markings. Our paint, our numbers. One of them was a tail I cleared for departure in March.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The quartermaster found a case under Teal's bunk. A coffee tin, twelve tapes, and a note: 'For Sera. Not for the net.'

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Keep these off the command net. Somebody up there is listening and signing things they shouldn't. If I go quiet, the case goes to Sera. Only Sera.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: The manifest sends grain drums to a farm with a runway, then five quays on Iron Coast. Nobody ships grain in drums.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: There are real houses in that yard. Families who work the siding. I need you to come home with the right number of fires.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Iron Coast is a hundred miles of our own shoreline. Whoever this is, they're not invading. They're already home.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Then I'll look at that farm. From above, before anyone can tidy it up.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: I dropped beacons on the way in. Low power, my own frequency. If anyone ever follows me, I wanted it to be someone who knew the song.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He used to tune that pass on Sundays. Said it was the only place the tower couldn't talk to him.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Recovery followed the beacons into the snowy pass. His receiver was in the rocks. Cracked case, memory intact. He meant us to find it.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: There's a radar inside our own training box. Dug into the bowl north of the pass. Nobody signed for it. I checked the ledger three times.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Somebody wanted to watch trainees. Not the sky. Trainees. Think about why you'd want to know when the kids fly.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: If it's real, it's been watching every pattern you've flown for a year. Command wants it gone quietly. I want it photographed first.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: If I just blow it up, it's a rumour. If I look at it first, it's a crime.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: The Teklan farmers let me hide a tape in a seed tin. The old woman asked my name, not my rank. Nobody at Varda has asked my name in ten years.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The radar's memory names that orchard. Three days later somebody ordered it evacuated. Now there are patrols firing on the evacuation trucks.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: They're not shooting at farmers. They're shooting at a seed tin. That's how badly someone wants Teal's tape back.

transcript.speaker: RUSK
transcript.text: ...three officers at Varda are being reassigned tonight. Their names are already off the roster. Nobody will ask. Nobody ever asks.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: The couriers carry patrol routes high over the orchard hills. Their crews guide the guns onto the trucks.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Three transports above the hills, with escorts hidden by two jammers. Find the transports and the families have a road out.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Those trucks are carrying somebody who asked his name. They get out.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The convoy made it. The old woman's granddaughter drove the lead truck. She marked three silos on the map with her thumb. 'Those smell wrong.'

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Three tanks under grain permits. Aviation fuel. The farmers know the difference, they just can't prove it. A fuel ledger would prove it.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Sparrow. Every unmarked silo in that valley is somebody's winter. Don't be the one who makes them hungry to make a point.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He wrote that one for you. He never wrote anything for me. I'm choosing not to be hurt by that today.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Vulture Lead followed me into the pass. He wasn't chasing a deserter. You don't chase deserters at night with your lights off. He was erasing a witness.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: If the fuel burns, he'll come looking for you over the works. You don't owe him a duel. Bring yourself home.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Three thumbprints. Three fires. Then I'm leaving him in the dark.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: You got clear of Vulture Lead. His orders kept repeating on guard; we recorded them. Every one bears a governor's name. He died in spring.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Kiro talks to Lira. Lira talks to Merel. Merel talks to the harbours. Start at the quays; listen back up the chain.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: I wiped his name off my board this morning. Then I wrote it back. I'm not ready to decide what he is.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: On the coast, look at what the cranes unload. The uniforms tell you nothing. The crates do.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Iron Coast. Military stores beside a fish market. The Marshal put his war where he knew we'd hesitate.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Workers are two blocks from those quays. The ships and tankers are his supply line. Their neighbours are not.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: He's right. I'll hesitate. Then I'll aim.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Kiro keeps an archive. Every forged order, filed, because forgers are vain. It's the only honest thing on the plateau.

transcript.speaker: RUSK
transcript.text: Declare the emergency first. Find the reason after. In a year, nobody has asked me for the reason.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The harbour traffic gave us Kiro's signing key. A key alone is a rumour. We need Lira and Merel's logs with the same signature.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Lira and Merel sit on opposite ridges and hate each other's weather. Lira lies, Merel repeats her. The west ridge still hears the farms.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Three logs, one signature. Send them home to Varda. Its island transmitter can reach the farms without borrowing his voice.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: I came home through the pass. Not the pretty way. The way you take when you don't want to be seen coming home.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: His own words, in his own voice, on their own relay. He'd have liked that.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Three stations, one signature. Varda's island transmitter has the orders and the governor's death certificate. Thirty-five seconds.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: A clear signal needs time. Don't give them a hero. Give them thirty-five seconds and a hero is beside the point.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He recorded that two weeks before he vanished. Thirty-five seconds. He'd already timed it. He knew exactly what this would take.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: I'm staying in the tower. In case you were wondering. I'm not leaving my chair for them.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Keep the lights on, Sera. I'll keep the sky.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Three garrisons heard it. Two stood down. Their people are coming ashore to join us.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Three loyalist frigates cover the landing under the weather. The command ship carries a green beacon and most of our hope.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Storms ground frightened people. They don't ground orders, or fuel, or the people who own them. When the weather's bad, that's when they move.
